newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares in slump at start of bourse dealings.
newsitem.headline: German shares in slump at start of bourse dealings.

text.p: German shares were in a slump on Monday, hurt by profit-taking after the DAX index on Friday surged to a new all-time high on buying tied to the expiry of DAX futures and options and stock options.
The 30-share DAX was down 18.90 points at 3,769.37 points but off the session low reached in early trade at 3,755.44.

"It looks like we are set for a period of light consolidation," said one Frankfurt-based trader. "This appears to be profit-taking but it is nothing severe. This is an issue for today in the market, not the start of a correction."
The DAX index should find support at 3,760 points on any selling waves, with further support evident at 3,740 points.
Traders also said the market lacks the momentum to make a run toward resistance at 3,790 points and to break the psychologically-important 3,800-point level on Monday.

"We had a big expiry on Friday and the market is trying to find its feet," said another Frankfurt share trader. "But I would be surprised if the DAX fell below 3,760 points. There's not enough drive to push the market in either direction."
The usual factors, a surging U.S. share market and the dollar stabile above 1.70 marks, helped underpin the DAX.
Among specific shares, telephone group Deutsche Telekom was up 35 pfennigs at 43 marks.

Telekom denied a weekend report that it planned to dismiss board member Herbert May in the next few weeks after talks over allowing other telecoms firms access to Deutsche's network broke down. May is responsible for business clients at Telekom.
One trading house said pharmaceuticals group Bayer AG, industrial group Daimler-Benz AG and electronics group Siemens AG were in favour due to technical factors.
Bayer was down 96 pfennigs at 68.70 marks and Daimler was down 40 pfennigs at 136.40 marks, while Siemens was up 1.05 marks at 102.70 marks.
German television network Pro Sieben on Monday also set the bookbuilding price range for its initial offering of preference shares at 66 to 72 marks per share.
The network said the offering could lead to a market capitalisation of up to 2.5 billion marks.
